title: The workshop as a temple: telepathic playing and the arts together
summary: He describes the room as a place to pray in music, with collective improvisation and a sense of one mind, and the plan to join photography and painting with music.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: but more like a temple or a place to come and bathe yourself in music and to pray in music. And when we did play in that room, not only were the musicians very telepathic, but many, many times, and as a listener, if you were there, I'm sure you may have experienced the same thing, where sometimes we would be transported to a zone where it felt like the whole room was of one mind and the music was happening right there. Because a great majority of what we played was happening on the spot, even though it might have been a conventional composition or a standard tune, we would go to new and fresh places almost every time we played. But it sounded like something that we might have worked on for months and months and months to get together. And the people just seemed like they would travel with us. And I remember many times just being lost in sound and lost in space and lost in this embrace of people. I've never had musical experiences quite like that any other time in my life. I've had very profound experiences that happened, but that particular room had some very, very special things happening in it. And in the development of the concepts that I'm talking about, we saw that photography and all of the other arts were... Excuse me.
Can we get that out there, Brad?

Okay. We saw that photography and the other aspects of art could also be brought into that same kind of setting or to bring about a unity, a integration of music and photography, music and painting, the way the mural expressed it. The mural that Eugene Ray designed, for example, was singing all the time or playing all the time. And it was something that was done, but it seemed to fit the mood and the moment or the magic of everything that was happening.
